thread:
julia (support): FYI — ACME hitting big p99 spike starting ~11:10 UTC. p95 up ~4x, p99 up ~20x. Errors: repeated 503 with 'OOM during kv_alloc' and intermittent 401s on billing token exchange. Customer reports timeouts + retries. Can we triage?
ryan (eng-runtime): do we have tenant id + route? model + max_tokens? any change in rollout?
julia (support): tenant=acme-corp-42, route=prod-us-east-1/gpt-open-v2, model=redwood-open-13b, max_tokens=8192 for some sessions. No explicit rollout from our side. Logs snippet from their last failed request: ```2024-05-12T11:12:03Z error request_id=... kv_alloc: allocation failed: OOM
2024-05-12T11:12:03Z warn token_service: 401 token_exchange failed, retrying```
maya (runtime): that combination (large max_tokens + long chat sessions) matches KV growth causing slab fragmentation. If allocator can't evict prefixes fast enough we see p99 bursts. Can we get allocator stats and kv size heatmap for that tenant?
anna (sre): I'm seeing correlated traces on pool-gpu-3 between 11:08-11:15 — sustained high slab fragmentation and low free contiguous ranges. Quick mitigation options: 1) route affected tenant to a smaller model variant (quantized) 2) enable aggressive kv-eviction for that tenant 3) soft-drain hot workers & let autoscaler bring fresh ones. Which do we want now?
julia (support): customer requests fastest fix. They prefer no model change if possible. They can tolerate brief throttling.
ryan (eng-runtime): short-term: add an active fallback route to redwood-open-7b-quant for that tenant and throttle concurrency to 2 per-tenant. I'll push a routing rule. @deploy-bot can you do the route change?
deploy-bot: rollout started: fallback-route=redwood-open-7b-quant -> targeting acme-corp-42, change id=rb-171823, will complete in ~30s.
maya (runtime): while that's rolling, ops to trigger slab compaction on impacted workers (non-disruptive compaction). Commands to run on worker node (careful): ```# check allocator stats curl -s http://localhost:9090/allocator/stats | jq .
# trigger compaction (safe compaction endpoint) curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/allocator/compact```
anna (sre): I'm going to cordon & drain 1 hot worker from pool-gpu-3, let new instance join. `kubectl cordon node/gpu-3-21 && kubectl drain node/gpu-3-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
julia (support): billing-bot flagged spikes in failed token exchanges earlier — could auth retries be amplifying the load?
billing-bot: we saw a burst of 401s for tenant acme-corp-42 between 11:09-11:13 due to intermittent KMS latency; most requests retried x2-x3 which increased sustained concurrency. Root cause looks external but amplified allocator pressure. Logged under billing-incident-1718.
maya (runtime): that combination (auth retries + long contexts) is classic multiplier: more open sessions => more KV entries held => fragmentation. Good catch.
ryan (eng-runtime): mitigation checklist summarized: 1) fallback routing to 7b quant (done, deploy id rb-171823) 2) throttle per-tenant concurrency to 2 (applied) 3) run allocator compact on warm workers (in progress) 4) cordon/drain hot node (anna doing) 5) ask billing to follow up on token exchange reliability w/ KMS (billing-bot)
anna (sre): compaction request returned 200 on 3 nodes. Node drain finished, new worker ready. Pool metrics: slab fragmentation dropped ~60% in 2 mins, p99 for tenant down from ~3.2s -> ~380ms so far.
julia (support): shared update with customer: we routed traffic to a smaller quantized model + throttled concurrency; we're performing node compaction & rotation; billing team investigating token 401s. Customer says they're OK with this for now but wants follow-up RCA.
ryan (eng-runtime): next steps: collect allocator stats pre/post for RCA, collect flamegraphs for p99 traces, and propose allocator tuning (eviction aggressiveness, slab compaction cadence) to prevent recurrence. @maya can you own RCA?
maya (runtime): I'll own RCA. Plan: gather allocator stats, KV growth timelines, and correlate with billing 401 window. Will propose config changes: lower max cached prefixes for long sessions, and a per-tenant slab thermostat threshold.
julia (support): thanks team. I'll file a customer postmortem and share timeline + mitigation steps. Follow-up meeting? 30 mins after logs fully collected. :thumbsup:
anna (sre): thumbs up. I'll attach node IDs and compaction traces to the ticket.
deploy-bot: rollout rb-171823 completed successfully at 1718234625.
billing-bot: opened billing ticket BT-171823 for KMS retries, assigned to ops-ryan.
julia (support): closing interim update — monitoring for 15m then update ACME.
anna (sre): monitoring shows stable p99 at ~350-420ms for the tenant. moving this to postmortem queue. :white_check_mark:
